claim.value: Incomplete follow-up can leave the release effect uncertain.
claim.scope: A possible limitation, not a finding that follow-up is incomplete.

provenance.rationale: The span explicitly identifies incomplete follow-up as a possible source of uncertainty about the release effect.

signal_basis.value: Compare the proportion reaching a traceable first publication within the predefined observation window, following unresolved histories and separately reporting accounts whose publication opportunity has not occurred.
signal_basis.scope: The mapping proposes these observations for the release evaluation; their occurrence is assumed for this assessment, rather than reported as a completed finding.

provenance.rationale: The cited spans supply the outcome, observation window, treatment of unresolved histories and pending opportunities, and proposed status of the observations.
The claim is supported without requiring an unresolved empirical relation.

rationale: Incomplete follow-up can leave relevant publication outcomes unresolved and therefore leave uncertainty about the release effect, even when an observed publication difference is available. This licenses the stated possible limitation without establishing that follow-up actually is incomplete.
uncertainty: The claim does not specify whether incomplete follow-up occurs or how much uncertainty it would introduce.
